bib.title: A Watermark for Large Language Models

question: Can LLM output be watermarked at generation time, without retraining, so that a short span is detectable with a rigorous p-value and without access to the model?
hypothesis: Softly boosting a pseudo-random green list of tokens yields a detectable watermark with negligible quality cost, and detection sensitivity depends on the entropy of the text.
contributions: Hard and soft green/red list watermark with a z-test detector
Spike-entropy based sensitivity analysis (Theorem 4.2) and perplexity bound (Theorem 4.3)
Experiments with OPT-1.3B and an attack study

method.summary: At each step a hash of the previous token seeds a PRNG that splits the vocabulary into a green list (fraction gamma) and a red list; delta is added to green logits before sampling. Detection counts green tokens and applies a one-proportion z-test, needing no model access. Tested on OPT-1.3B with C4 realnewslike prompts.

datasets.name: C4 realnewslike
datasets.size: at least 500 generations with T=200+-5 tokens per setting (500+-10 sequences)
datasets.split: random selection of texts; fixed number of tokens trimmed from the end as human baseline completion, rest is prompt
datasets.preprocessing: EOS suppressed for greedy and beam search, sequences truncated to T=200

inference.decoding: multinomial sampling, greedy decoding, and beam search (4 and 8 beams, greedy over beams)
inference.samples: about 500 generations per parameter setting; single run, no seeds stated
inference.prompting: prompt = C4 text with trailing tokens removed; TriviaQA zero-shot template (see prompts)

parameters.hash: one previous token (h=1) seeds torch RNG in experiments
parameters.T5 attack: k=20 candidates via 50-way beam search, replacement budget eps in 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7

other.implementation: PyTorch backend of Huggingface generate API with logit warping

metrics.name: type-I/II error (FPR/FNR, TPR, TNR)
metrics.definition: at z thresholds 4 and 5 over about 500 generations

metrics.name: perplexity (PPL)
metrics.definition: exp of mean token loss of OPT-2.7B on generated tokens given the prompt

eval.protocol: Each setting about 500 sequences of T=200+-5; no repeated seeds or confidence intervals reported.

results.claim: Soft watermark detects 98.4% of OPT-1.3B generations at z=4 with multinomial sampling and 99.6% with 4-way beam search.
results.setup: OPT-1.3B, C4 realnewslike, T=200, gamma=0.5, delta=2.0, about 500 generations
results.quote:
Empirically, 98.4% of generations
are detected at the z = 4 (128 token) threshold when multi-
nomial sampling is used.

results.claim: At z=4 the false positive rate is 3e-5 by theory and no false positives were observed in any run.
results.setup: gamma, delta grid in Table 2, about 500 generations per row
results.note: Table 2 caption: a maximum of one type-I error was observed for any given run; text near Table 2 says none were observed.

results.claim: Table 2: delta=2.0, gamma=0.5 multinomial gives TPR 0.984 at z=4.
results.table: Table 2, row m-nom. delta 2.0 gamma 0.50, column z=4.0 TPR (0.984)

results.claim: Table 2: delta=1.0, gamma=0.5 multinomial gives TPR only 0.767 at z=4 and 0.504 at z=5.
results.table: Table 2, row m-nom. delta 1.0 gamma 0.50, column z=4.0 TPR (0.767)

results.claim: Theorem 4.2 lower bound on expected green tokens was 142.2 and the empirical mean was 159.5.
results.setup: OPT-1.3B, 200 tokens, gamma=0.5, delta=2, mean spike entropy S=0.807
results.quote:
Theorem 4.2 says that the expected number of green list
tokens per generation is at least 142.2. Indeed, the empiri-
cal average is 159.5.

results.claim: A small green list gamma=0.1 is pareto-optimal for z-score vs perplexity under multinomial sampling.
results.quote: Interestingly, we see that a small green list, γ = .1 is pareto-optimal.

results.claim: With 8-way beam search a watermark of delta=2 reaches average z>5 within 35 tokens, at very low PPL cost.
results.quote:
an average
z-score greater than 5 is achieved for as few as 35 tokens

results.claim: A T5-Large span replacement attack with budget 0.1 cuts AUC by 0.01 but at 0.3 budget it triples PPL.
results.quote:
we only measure a decrease
in watermark strength of 0.01 AUC when ε = 0.1

results.claim: Table 8: after T5 attack with eps=0.3 multinomial TPR@4 falls from 0.984 to 0.353 (FNR 0.647).
results.table: Table 8, row m-nom. eps 0.3, column w/attck TPR@4.0 (0.353)

results.claim: Table 8: at eps=0.7 multinomial TPR@4 under attack is 0.039; beam search holds 0.299.
results.table: Table 8, row m-nom. eps 0.7, column w/attck TPR@4.0 (0.039)
results.note: Attack effect is larger than the 'degrades gracefully' framing in the Conclusion suggests at high budgets, though PPL rises to 33.9 (Fig 6).

results.claim: Removing the watermark from a long hard-watermarked sequence requires modifying roughly one quarter of tokens or more.
results.setup: analysis, T=1000, adversary modifies 200 tokens, hard red list
results.quote:
In general, removing the watermark of a
long sequence requires modifying roughly one quarter of
the tokens or more.

results.claim: z=4 threshold gives one-sided p about 3e-5 and a hard watermark is detectable from 16 tokens.
results.quote:
we will detect
any watermarked sequence with 16 or more tokens

results.claim: On TriviaQA, soft watermark (gamma 0.5, delta 2) lowers flan-ul2 EM from 0.374 to 0.336.
results.table: Table 9, row google/flan-ul2, column EM (W) (0.336 vs EM 0.374)

results.claim: TriviaQA drop in EM under watermark was under 4 points for both models.
results.quote: We observe less than a 4 point drop in Exact Match performance

results.claim: Authors state detection is unreliable on low entropy text such as memorized or templated content.
results.quote: Anecdotally, failure cases typically seem to involve data memorization

limits: Evaluated mainly on OPT-1.3B (and one OPT-6.7B figure); no large instruction-tuned chat model for the main results
Single run per setting, about 500 samples, no confidence intervals
Only text form is watermarked: a new essay written from an LM outline is not detectable (Appendix B)
Low entropy and memorized text cannot be watermarked and is the main source of false negatives
Strong attacks (emoji, generative, paraphrase at high budget) can defeat it; authors suggest instruction tuning against them
TriviaQA factuality test is acknowledged as a worst case and not a deployment setting
Theory assumes uniformly random red list, not the seeded PRNG used in practice
Aaronson/OpenAI scheme not compared because details were unavailable
